hints: Notice the question asks about the elastic limit on a stress-strain graph, not the limit of proportionality where Hooke's law stops.
Recall that below the elastic limit unloading returns the material to zero strain, while above it some permanent plastic strain remains.
Check the direction words in each phrase - decide whether plastic behaviour happens below the limit or only once strain is increased above the limit.
walkthrough: Start from the meaning of the elastic limit: it is the strain up to which the material behaves elastically and will return to its original length when stress is removed.
Distinguish it from the limit of proportionality: Hooke's law with stress proportional to strain stops at the limit of proportionality, which is at or slightly before the elastic limit.

Apply the elastic versus plastic rule: for strains smaller than the elastic limit the deformation is elastic, and for strains larger than the elastic limit part of the deformation is plastic and remains after unloading.

Translate this into maximum-below and minimum-above language: the elastic limit is the largest strain that is still fully elastic, which is the same point as the smallest strain that produces plastic deformation.
That description matches the minimum strain above which the deformation is plastic. This is option D

options.A: This describes the limit of proportionality, where stress is still proportional to strain, which occurs at or before the elastic limit.
options.B: This reverses the physics - below the elastic limit the deformation is elastic and reversible, not plastic.
options.C: Hooke's law is obeyed below the limit of proportionality, not above the elastic limit where behaviour becomes non-linear and permanent.
options.D: Above the elastic limit the material does not return to its original length, so deformation becomes plastic and permanent.
